extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit organizations, community program staff, and grant writers seeking public or private funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing competitive grant proposals for community/nonprofit programs, covering need statements, measurable objectives, methodology, evaluation, budgeting, matching share, cash flow, sustainability, and appendices. Geared toward organizations seeking state, federal, foundation, or corporate support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem/Need Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe why your constituency needs assistance (not why your organization needs money). Convince the funding source that the problems are serious but not insurmountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local sources of information; use national data only to compare local situation to national outlook. Funders appreciate statistical and comparative data but do not appreciate being overwhelmed with data. Never paint a picture so terrible that there is no hope of solving it. Know what other experts and program operators are doing and develop linkages with outside groups and organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present a Single, Optimal Solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide one option for tackling the problem — the final, most optimal solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide multiple competing options. The proposal should pick and defend the chosen approach as the preferred remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives: measurable and client-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives describe the desired end product or situation at the conclusion of the project and should be stated in measurable, quantifiable terms from the client's point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives are the traceable link between the problem description and goods/services provided. They are terminal (what clients will look like at project conclusion) and focus organizational activity. Objectives generally fall into input, process and impact categories. Remember five essential parts: What (action verb), Who (target group), Where (geographic/place), When (target date or schedule), and What extent (quality/quantity measurement). Distinguish objectives from activities (methods) and goals (broad, long-range statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methods (strategies, activities, or procedures) to be employed to accomplish the objectives, including what you are doing and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: what activities are; justification for actions; flow of activities and time to get results; target population characteristics and selection process; staff requirements (hiring/training); start-up activities prior to full implementation. Best proposals also describe Design (case study, pilot, controlled experiment, etc.), Population Recruitment (projected participants and selection and their role in planning), Treatment (sufficient procedural detail), Reporting and Participant Tracking (how info will be collected and by whom; include special instruments in appendix), Management (administrative structure and functions), and Time Schedule (approximate timeline; charts useful but must be cogent). Develop activities in chronological order and consider backward chaining (list final step first then preceding steps). Ensure methodology flows from objectives; include a timetable to help reviewers analyze sequence and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan (data collection and monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how data will be collected, progress monitored and analyzed and the types of evaluation to be conducted (product and/or process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how records will be kept; identify the evaluator by name, title, credentials and extent of impartiality; outline reporting procedures; provide specific due dates for completing evaluation activities. Demonstrate interest in upgrading the project and enable funders to measure progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product evaluation (goal/objective achievement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product evaluation measures success in meeting project objectives and examines degree of success in attaining short-term program goals and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantifiable measures to assess program success relative to program needs, design efficiency, and expenditures (cost efficiency). Examples: reduced costs per participant, increased proportion of parents in training, reduction in welfare, planned vs actual expenditures, percent placed in jobs, number placed in unsubsidized jobs, increased average hourly wage of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process evaluation (methods and cost-effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process evaluation measures the methods used toward the goal and answers whether the benefit of actions was worth the cost and whether actions met higher goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether methods were carried out as planned, their efficiency, and their contribution to outcomes; include measures that can be observed directly (workload, capacity, complexity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate post-program success measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures based on clients' history to evaluate short-term outcomes after program participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include increased employment or reduced unemployment, increased earnings, increased labor force participation, reduced dependency on government, mobility of labor force, and jobs filled in target areas or occupational categories. Also examples like increased proportion leaving welfare, dollar volume of grant reductions, number of registrants entering employment, and increased employability measures (attitude towards work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program operating efficiency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Gauges that directly observe program functions to arrive at conclusions about efficiency of program activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicative measures relate to workload, capacity for work, and mix/complexity of activities. Examples: increase intake by X percent over fiscal year to a total of Y; increase number of tests administered to a total of Z. Use such measures to assess how well program activity was performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: clear statement and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget must explicitly state what the organization needs (total project cost) and support each item in the budget. Provide a budget summary and detailed justification showing requested amount, organization contribution and other outside sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders often cannot tell what is needed if the budget is unclear. Support each budget item in the narrative. Keep the budget section concise; a long presentation often demonstrates poor organization. Do not inflate the budget — funders generally fund to the penny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of typical budget line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide carefully documented cost details for standard budget categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and itemize the following as applicable: Salaries and Wages (list each staff position with title, salary range, number of persons, months/weeks on project, percent time, total per position); Fringe Benefits (list and compute FICA, unemployment, workers’ comp, hospitalization, provide computation and rate details); Consultant and Contractual Services (list fees and provide cost breakouts for each item; include legal/accounting/professional services and secondary recipients); Space Costs (rent, utilities, janitorial, maintenance; show amount per month × project months or cost per square footage; consider cost analysis or simplified methods); Equipment Purchases (non-expendable personal property > $300 and >1 year life; include transport/installation/lease-to-purchase provisions and check funder policy limits); Equipment Rental (list each item and monthly rental fee; check funder policy); Consumable Supplies; Utilities (if separated from space costs); Travel (transportation, meals, lodging per funder policy — project mileage and purpose for each staff, specify out-of-state travel purpose and check allowability); Telecommunications (installation and monthly charges for phones, fax, mobile, data lines); Program Income (direct charges/fees to participants must be kept in restricted account and used per funder rules); Special Project Costs (meals, training manuals, printing — show specific cost details); Other Costs (postage, maintenance, meeting costs, insurance — provide breakouts); Overhead/Indirect Costs (apply approved indirect rate or fixed percentage; avoid duplication; check whether funder disallows such charges and whether a cost allocation plan is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching share (cash and in-kind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching share represents the portion of project costs not borne by the funding source and may be a required minimum for government programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching can consist of charges incurred by grantee, cash contributions from other sources, and services/property donated by others. Cash contributions examples: salaries & fringe, travel, postage, office supplies, new equipment (with prior approval). In-kind contributions include value of donated services, real or personal property, or use thereof that directly benefit the project. Volunteer services may be counted if integral and necessary — value at rates consistent with similar work in the market; services provided by another employer valued at the employee's regular rate (exclusive of fringe/overhead) if same skill. Donated expendable personal property values should not exceed fair market value at time of donation. For donated nonexpendable property/buildings/land: if grant purpose is to furnish facility, full value may be claimed; if purpose is usage, depreciation or use charges may be made. Values cannot exceed fair market value of comparable items; donated space cannot exceed fair rental value as established by appraisal; loaned equipment value cannot exceed fair rental value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow management
rubrics_metrics.description: Address both the relationship between the organization's disbursement needs and the funding agency's reimbursement process, and monthly tracking of actual versus planned expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine cash needs for each period (start-up, monthly allotments) and for each project. Understand funder disbursement methods (reimbursement vouchers vs periodic grants or letters of credit). Prepare and send vouchers and disbursements timely and ensure proper preparation. Monitor cash flows in every line item to prevent overruns or idleness of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future funding / sustainability planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain plans for sustaining the project after the funding period and the prospects for spin-off or continued operation without outside funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether the project can become free-standing, plans to seek future funding from same or other sources, and implications if outside support declines. Estimate next-year operating costs by analyzing past costs and accounting for inflation, cost-of-living/pay increases, retirement/vacation/fringe changes, changes in taxes/insurance/audits/postage and rent. Demonstrate realistic planning for continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix contents and packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Include supporting documents commonly required in an appendix and present them in a neat, orderly, and clearly labeled fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common appendix items: copy of organization's 501(c)(3) IRS letter; list of board members with addresses/phone numbers; most recent audit report, current financial statement and operating budget; annual report; resumes of key project staff; letters of support from community organizations; news clippings/releases highlighting achievements; organizational brochures. Number and clearly label each Appendix and refer to Appendix numbers in the proposal body to help reviewers find required documents easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funding-source policies and reference resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the specific funding source's policies before including items (equipment limits, travel allowances, indirect costs, matching share rules, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handbook references directories and publications (e.g., Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance, Foundation Directory, corporate giving directories) as resources for finding funders and for learning program-specific restrictions, eligibility, deadlines and application procedures. Use these resources to align proposal content and budget with funder requirements.
